newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bad weather delays Romania farm works, crops safe.
newsitem.headline: Bad weather delays Romania farm works, crops safe.

text.p: Seasonal work in Romania's farming sector has been delayed by heavy rainfalls and snow over the past week, but the 1997 crops should be unaffected by the adverse weather, a government official said.
"So far, we received no signals saying the bad weather has affected crops," said Elena Coreico, a spokeswoman for the Agriculture Ministry.
Heavy rain and snowfalls have hit Romania over the past week, submerging large areas and preventing farmers from continuing seasonal work.
Coreico said of the 5.77 million hectares planned for spring sowing of all crops, only 468,300 ha, or 8.0 percent, had been sown so far.
"However, we hope to recoup the delays once the weather improves," she said.

A total of 3.13 million ha will be put under maize, 782,000 ha under sunflower and 138,401 ha under sugar beet, roughly the same as the 1996 figures. The remainder is given over to technical plants and fodder.
Coreico said maize sowing had not been delayed as it usually started by the end of April in the Balkan country.
Reports in the media said rivers in southern and northern Romania had flooded scores of households and plots of farmland.
"Some areas are still under water, but the temperatures are low so those crops are not in danger. Farmers have already started to drain the water," Coreico said.
She said rainfall over the past week had been "a blessing" after a dry winter, especially in the southern and western areas put under wheat last autumn.
The weather was expected to improve across the country over the next days, weathermen said on Tuesday.
Coreico said the weather plus a shortage of funds were behind slow distribution of fuel and fertilisers.
Ministry data showed of the 86,000 tonnes of fuel needed this month only 2,534 tonnes had been supplied so far and that from the necessary 117,671 tonnes of fertilisers some 1,602 were distributed.
Last month, the government said it would give 550 billion lei in subsidised credits to enable farmers to finance seasonal work.
It also said farmers could get fresh credits even if they failed to repay old loans.

Last week, the state-run National Oil Company (CRP) said it would start distribution of fuel to the farming sector and asked for payment 30 days after delivery, in a bid to help the cash-strapped sector.
